chunks: And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala') from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Muhrim (person in Ihram) does not remove lice from his body or his garment intentionally; and if he kills any of them by mistake, he should feed in its place a handful of food with his hand.
And there is no harm if he takes what is other than lice from his body; and if he wishes to move the lice from one place to another, he may do so and there is no penalty upon him. Narrated.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (consecration)
key_terms.فِيهَا: In its place (referring to the fidya payment)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a Muhrim who accidentally kills a louse?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlighting the juristic distinction between intentional removal (which is prohibited but carries no expiation) and accidental killing (which requires a fidya of feeding a handful of food). This hadith clarifies that the penalty is specific to the destruction of the louse, allowing the pilgrim to move them without incurring liability, thereby balancing ritual purity with practical comfort during Hajj.
